channel.title: Paste Media Group - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Paste Media Group (pastemagazine.com)

item.title: Jonathan Bernstein on the life and legacy of Justin Townes Earle
item.description: Audio Books: The Rolling Stone journalist speaks with Paste about the art of fact-checking, handling sensitive stories with care, and authoring What Do You Do When You’re Lonesome: The Authorized Biography of Justin Townes Earle.

item.title: Nothing's momentum stalls on a short history of decay
item.description: The Philly outfit has rightfully inspired an entire generation of like-minded shoegaze and post-hardcore bands, but they sound occasionally uninspired themselves on their fifth record and Run for Cover debut.

item.title: Gorillaz struggle to reach their emotional peak on The Mountain
item.description: Inspired by a visit to India, Damon Albarn and Jamie Hewlett ground their musings on the afterlife in warm, gorgeous instrumentation with a clear, cohesive thematic anchor, but the style ultimately overwhelms the substance.

item.title: The beautiful, bloated chaos of The 1975's second album
item.description: Revisiting the band's maximalist, neon, sprawling I like it when you sleep, for you are so beautiful yet so unaware of it 10 years later means reckoning with who we were when instability was a frontman’s most valuable currency.

item.title: Nobody asked for a Gnarls Barkley reunion
item.description: CeeLo Green and Danger Mouse’s mid-2000s collab was fun back in the day, but the statements Green made about rape victims in 2014 loom heavily over the project.

item.title: 5 songs you need to hear this week
item.description: This week’s best new songs roundup features Grace Ives’ fizzy synth-pop, Heather the Jerk’s old-world garage-punk, and Swapmeet’s woozy, overdriven blur.

item.title: Money wins again, as Netflix drops its Warner Bros. acquisition dreams
item.description: Netflix has declined to try to match Paramount's most recent "superior" offer, and has dropped out of the race to buy Warner Bros. Discovery.

item.title: Library of Congress finds cinema's previously lost "first robot"
item.description: Long considered lost, George Méliès' "Gugusse And The Automaton" has finally been rediscovered.
